source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: When the suffix attached is –LA-N, only one external argument may be added. The addition of the reflexive suffix –n to –LAA prevents further projection of arguments other than the external one. In particular, no accusative internal argument may be licensed4. That the sole argument of LA-N-verbs is merged externally testifying to their unergative status is witnessed from the fact that LA-N verbs can undergo causativization and passivization – two operations which require the presence of an external argument and which are therefore banned with unaccusative verbs.
en: Life made Misha come to his senses.
